segments.text: Regular prose is what most of an entry looks like.
Sentences go here without any decoration, and that is the happy path most readers see.
You can emphasise a word with bold or italic, and the two compose into bold italic when you need to be emphatic about emphasis.
Inline code stays monospace and breaks out of the reading font so the reader's eye catches it.
Links like Cloudflare open in a new tab by convention.
Strikethrough via ~~text~~ becomes rendered text — useful for showing edits, corrections, or crossed-out mistakes without removing the original content.
The TTS narrator skips struck-through content by default so listeners hear the intended reading, not the redaction.
The acronym Cascading Style Sheets is read as "cascading style sheets" when the text-to-speech narrator encounters it, not as three spelled-out letters.
Accessible Rich Internet Applications and Cross-Origin Resource Sharing behave the same way.
